raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-UK-HyNetCCUSCluster",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Network under‑utilisation if build‑out projects fail to take FID, reducing user fees and revenue for the T&SCo.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Secure firm take‑or‑pay commitments, include penalty clauses, and allow regulator to disallow CapEx for non‑signed projects.",
      "evidence": "risk that if one or more of the build‑out projects ... fails to take FID, the network ... will be underutilised (section 4.2.2)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Cost overruns on the T&S network construction exceeding the allowed capital allowance.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Apply cost‑sharing factor, regulator caps, rigorous cost assurance and contingency budgeting.",
      "evidence": "Eni T&S network construction overruns; any overruns subject to cost sharing, recoup only 40% (section 4.1.3, 5.7.11)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Discontinuation of EETH or Protos leading to loss of revenue and stranded assets.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Include discontinuation agreements with compensation, monitor milestones and enforce performance penalties.",
      "evidence": "Discontinuation risk for EETH and Protos (section 5.7.4)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Shortfall in the de‑commissioning fund for the T&S network.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish a dedicated de‑commissioning fund with regular financial reviews and regulator oversight.",
      "evidence": "Decommissioning fund shortfall (section 5.7.5)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "CO₂ leakage from storage sites causing environmental damage and liability.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Deploy robust monitoring, sentinel wells, strict operational standards and SCA insurance coverage.",
      "evidence": "Government will underwrite high‑impact, low‑probability CO₂ leakage risks via the Supplementary Compensation Agreement (SCA) (section 1.3)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Regulatory changes by Ofgem to allowed revenue or rate of return affecting T&SCo financial model.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Secure a long‑term regulatory framework with flexibility clauses and periodic review mechanisms.",
      "evidence": "Ofgem sets allowed revenue and reviews it periodically (section 1.3, 4.4.2)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Delays in achieving FID and COD increase costs and erode projected benefits.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Apply PERT/QSRA assurance, maintain a 6‑month COD tolerance, and enforce strict change‑control processes.",
      "evidence": "Schedule tolerance of 6 months delay to COD; schedule assurance uses PERT and QSRA (sections 6.4.2, 6.5.3)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Limited supplier capacity and capability could cause cost escalation and delivery delays.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Early supplier engagement, develop supply‑chain capacity, embed contingencies and monitor market conditions.",
      "evidence": "Critical success factors include supplier capacity and capability; cost increases linked to supply‑chain issues (section 3.2.1, 4.2)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Low UK ETS carbon price makes capture projects uneconomic, threatening financial viability.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide revenue‑support contracts (RSA, CfD‑type), monitor carbon price and adjust strike prices as needed.",
      "evidence": "Carbon Price is currently too low to incentivise deployment; business models cover difference between strike and reference price (sections 1.2, 4.1.4)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Cross‑chain risk: failure of capture projects reduces T&SCo utilisation and revenue.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Allocate cross‑chain risk to appropriate parties, use revenue‑support agreements and monitor project progress closely.",
      "evidence": "Government underwrites cross‑chain risks; cross‑chain risks outlined in commercial case (sections 1.3, 4.3)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Political shift could alter CCUS policy or subsidy levels, affecting project funding.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Align contracts with the Subsidy Control Act, maintain ministerial forum engagement, embed flexibility for policy changes.",
      "evidence": "Subsidy Control Act 2022 compliance and ministerial forum on CCUS (sections 4.2.5, 2.2.4)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Legal risk of non‑compliance with subsidy‑control principles leading to challenges.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Conduct pre‑referral assessments, work closely with SAU, document compliance evidence.",
      "evidence": "Assessment of each subsidy scheme will be submitted to the Subsidy Advice Unit (SAU) (section 4.2.5)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Stakeholder opposition or safety concerns could delay permitting and construction.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Early community engagement, safety communication, and delivery of local benefits programmes.",
      "evidence": "Stakeholder engagement and communications approach includes community engagement and safety (section 6.2)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Inadequate data sharing between T&SCo, LCCC and DESNZ may impair monitoring and reporting.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Define a data‑management strategy, formal data‑sharing agreements and regular audits.",
      "evidence": "DESNZ will define a longer‑term data management strategy; overlapping data flows noted (section 6.6)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Technical failure of dense‑phase upgrade or injection wells could limit capacity and availability.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Detailed engineering design, phased testing, independent technical assurance and contingency engineering.",
      "evidence": "Phase 2 includes dense phase upgrades; technical assurance has examined project technical details (sections 2.3.2, 4.3)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "High‑cost sensitivity could turn the project’s NPV negative under adverse cost scenarios.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Perform high/low sensitivity analyses, enforce strict cost controls, and secure additional funding buffers.",
      "evidence": "Option 1 NPV could be -£1.0bn in high‑cost scenario; sensitivity analysis shown (section 3.4.2)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R17",
      "description": "Potential air‑quality impacts from waste‑to‑energy facilities within the cluster.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Apply stringent emission controls, continuous air‑quality monitoring and compliance with standards.",
      "evidence": "Costs include potential for CO₂ leakage and environmental and air quality impacts (section 1.4)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R18",
      "description": "Geological uncertainty of offshore storage sites could affect long‑term storage integrity.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Conduct thorough site characterisation, install monitoring and sentinel wells, and develop contingency storage options.",
      "evidence": "CO₂ stored in deep geological formations such as depleted fields or saline aquifers; storage capacity in Liverpool Bay (sections 1.1, 2.3.1)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R19",
      "description": "Revenue Support Agreement (RSA) top‑up may be required if user fees fall short, stressing exchequer resources.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Secure minimum demand commitments, embed demand forecasts in contracts, and cap government top‑up exposure.",
      "evidence": "If shortfall in demand ... government will ‘top up’ fees through RSA (section 1.3)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R20",
      "description": "Complex multi‑agency governance could cause decision‑making delays and mis‑alignment.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Maintain clear governance structures, regular board meetings, defined escalation paths and documented responsibilities.",
      "evidence": "Multiple governance forums: NLT, T1B, PB, CCUS Senior Board (section 4.1.4)."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Network under‑utilisation if build‑out projects fail to take FID, reducing user fees and revenue for the T&SCo.
risks.mitigation: Secure firm take‑or‑pay commitments, include penalty clauses, and allow regulator to disallow CapEx for non‑signed projects.
risks.evidence: risk that if one or more of the build‑out projects ... fails to take FID, the network ... will be underutilised (section 4.2.2).

risks.description: Cost overruns on the T&S network construction exceeding the allowed capital allowance.
risks.mitigation: Apply cost‑sharing factor, regulator caps, rigorous cost assurance and contingency budgeting.
risks.evidence: Eni T&S network construction overruns; any overruns subject to cost sharing, recoup only 40% (section 4.1.3, 5.7.11).

risks.description: Discontinuation of EETH or Protos leading to loss of revenue and stranded assets.
risks.mitigation: Include discontinuation agreements with compensation, monitor milestones and enforce performance penalties.
risks.evidence: Discontinuation risk for EETH and Protos (section 5.7.4).

risks.description: Shortfall in the de‑commissioning fund for the T&S network.
risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated de‑commissioning fund with regular financial reviews and regulator oversight.
risks.evidence: Decommissioning fund shortfall (section 5.7.5).

risks.description: CO₂ leakage from storage sites causing environmental damage and liability.
risks.mitigation: Deploy robust monitoring, sentinel wells, strict operational standards and SCA insurance coverage.
risks.evidence: Government will underwrite high‑impact, low‑probability CO₂ leakage risks via the Supplementary Compensation Agreement (SCA) (section 1.3).

risks.description: Regulatory changes by Ofgem to allowed revenue or rate of return affecting T&SCo financial model.
risks.mitigation: Secure a long‑term regulatory framework with flexibility clauses and periodic review mechanisms.
risks.evidence: Ofgem sets allowed revenue and reviews it periodically (section 1.3, 4.4.2).

risks.description: Delays in achieving FID and COD increase costs and erode projected benefits.
risks.mitigation: Apply PERT/QSRA assurance, maintain a 6‑month COD tolerance, and enforce strict change‑control processes.
risks.evidence: Schedule tolerance of 6 months delay to COD; schedule assurance uses PERT and QSRA (sections 6.4.2, 6.5.3).

risks.description: Limited supplier capacity and capability could cause cost escalation and delivery delays.
risks.mitigation: Early supplier engagement, develop supply‑chain capacity, embed contingencies and monitor market conditions.
risks.evidence: Critical success factors include supplier capacity and capability; cost increases linked to supply‑chain issues (section 3.2.1, 4.2).

risks.description: Low UK ETS carbon price makes capture projects uneconomic, threatening financial viability.
risks.mitigation: Provide revenue‑support contracts (RSA, CfD‑type), monitor carbon price and adjust strike prices as needed.
risks.evidence: Carbon Price is currently too low to incentivise deployment; business models cover difference between strike and reference price (sections 1.2, 4.1.4).

risks.description: Cross‑chain risk: failure of capture projects reduces T&SCo utilisation and revenue.
risks.mitigation: Allocate cross‑chain risk to appropriate parties, use revenue‑support agreements and monitor project progress closely.
risks.evidence: Government underwrites cross‑chain risks; cross‑chain risks outlined in commercial case (sections 1.3, 4.3).

risks.description: Political shift could alter CCUS policy or subsidy levels, affecting project funding.
risks.mitigation: Align contracts with the Subsidy Control Act, maintain ministerial forum engagement, embed flexibility for policy changes.
risks.evidence: Subsidy Control Act 2022 compliance and ministerial forum on CCUS (sections 4.2.5, 2.2.4).

risks.description: Legal risk of non‑compliance with subsidy‑control principles leading to challenges.
risks.mitigation: Conduct pre‑referral assessments, work closely with SAU, document compliance evidence.
risks.evidence: Assessment of each subsidy scheme will be submitted to the Subsidy Advice Unit (SAU) (section 4.2.5).

risks.description: Stakeholder opposition or safety concerns could delay permitting and construction.
risks.mitigation: Early community engagement, safety communication, and delivery of local benefits programmes.
risks.evidence: Stakeholder engagement and communications approach includes community engagement and safety (section 6.2).

risks.description: Inadequate data sharing between T&SCo, LCCC and DESNZ may impair monitoring and reporting.
risks.mitigation: Define a data‑management strategy, formal data‑sharing agreements and regular audits.
risks.evidence: DESNZ will define a longer‑term data management strategy; overlapping data flows noted (section 6.6).

risks.description: Technical failure of dense‑phase upgrade or injection wells could limit capacity and availability.
risks.mitigation: Detailed engineering design, phased testing, independent technical assurance and contingency engineering.
risks.evidence: Phase 2 includes dense phase upgrades; technical assurance has examined project technical details (sections 2.3.2, 4.3).

risks.description: High‑cost sensitivity could turn the project’s NPV negative under adverse cost scenarios.
risks.mitigation: Perform high/low sensitivity analyses, enforce strict cost controls, and secure additional funding buffers.
risks.evidence: Option 1 NPV could be -£1.0bn in high‑cost scenario; sensitivity analysis shown (section 3.4.2).

risks.description: Potential air‑quality impacts from waste‑to‑energy facilities within the cluster.
risks.mitigation: Apply stringent emission controls, continuous air‑quality monitoring and compliance with standards.
risks.evidence: Costs include potential for CO₂ leakage and environmental and air quality impacts (section 1.4).

risks.description: Geological uncertainty of offshore storage sites could affect long‑term storage integrity.
risks.mitigation: Conduct thorough site characterisation, install monitoring and sentinel wells, and develop contingency storage options.
risks.evidence: CO₂ stored in deep geological formations such as depleted fields or saline aquifers; storage capacity in Liverpool Bay (sections 1.1, 2.3.1).

risks.description: Revenue Support Agreement (RSA) top‑up may be required if user fees fall short, stressing exchequer resources.
risks.mitigation: Secure minimum demand commitments, embed demand forecasts in contracts, and cap government top‑up exposure.
risks.evidence: If shortfall in demand ... government will ‘top up’ fees through RSA (section 1.3).

risks.description: Complex multi‑agency governance could cause decision‑making delays and mis‑alignment.
risks.mitigation: Maintain clear governance structures, regular board meetings, defined escalation paths and documented responsibilities.
risks.evidence: Multiple governance forums: NLT, T1B, PB, CCUS Senior Board (section 4.1.4).
